title: Arrowhead Vine ( Syngonium spp.) Indoor Care, Growing Tips & Plant Guide

paragraphs.heading: Arrowhead Vine Quick Grow Guide
paragraphs.text: Best Soil: Equal parts peat moss or coir, vermiculite, and perlite Light Level: Medium to bright indirect light; avoid direct sunlight Water: Allow the potting medium to slightly dry out between waterings Temperature: 65°F to 75°F with average to high humidity Size: Dwarf varieties stay under 2 feet tall; common varieties grow 3 to 6 feet tall Care Tip: Keep variegated varieties in bright light to maintain coloration; leaves will revert to solid green in low light Common Problems: Aphids, mealybugs, spider mites, bacterial diseases, and stem rot Pet Safety: Not pet safe

paragraphs.heading: How to Grow Arrowhead Vine Indoors
paragraphs.text: Arrowhead vine ( Syngonium spp.) is a popular tropical houseplant grown for its colorful foliage. The plant is highly adaptable making it a great choice for growing indoors. Learn how to grow, water, fertilize, and troubleshoot arrowhead vine while choosing the best species and cultivars.

paragraphs.heading: Arrowhead Vine Plant Information and Native Habit
paragraphs.text: Arrowhead vine is a vining plant in the Araceae family. Native to the tropical rainforests of Mexico, the Caribbean, and Central and South America.

paragraphs.heading: Arrowhead Vine Plant Information and Native Habit
paragraphs.text: In its juvenile form, arrowhead vine grows on the forest floor and produces triangular, heart-shaped, or arrowhead-shaped leaves.

paragraphs.heading: Arrowhead Vine Plant Information and Native Habit
paragraphs.text: As plants begin to climb trees and receive more light, they produce an intermediate leaf form with 3 leaflets. Mature plants produce highly divided foliage with 5 to 11 leaflets.

paragraphs.heading: Arrowhead Vine Plant Information and Native Habit
paragraphs.text: As plants mature, their petioles lengthen, and they can be trained on a moss pole, trellis, or bamboo stake.

paragraphs.heading: Arrowhead Vine Leaf Colors and Ornamental Features
paragraphs.text: Hybrid varieties sport variegation in combinations of pink, red, yellow, white and various shades of green.

paragraphs.heading: Best Indoor Light for Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Arrowhead vines are tolerant of low light but prefer medium to bright light.

paragraphs.heading: Best Indoor Light for Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Variegated varieties will maintain their coloration better with brighter light.

paragraphs.heading: Best Indoor Light for Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Locate plants in an east-facing window or a few feet away from a west-facing window.

paragraphs.heading: Best Indoor Light for Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: North-facing windows also work well, but leaf color may become dull.

paragraphs.heading: How to Water Arrowhead Vine Plants
paragraphs.text: Allow the potting media to dry out slightly between waterings.

paragraphs.heading: How to Water Arrowhead Vine Plants
paragraphs.text: For more information on how to properly water houseplants, see Indoor Plants-Watering (HGIC 1459) .

paragraphs.heading: Ideal Temperature and Humidity for Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Arrowhead vine tolerates average home temperatures and humidity levels.

paragraphs.heading: Humidity levels at 50% or higher
paragraphs.text: They will tolerate lower humidity levels.

paragraphs.heading: Best Fertilizer for Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Arrowhead vines are not heavy feeders and should not be fertilized often if trying to keep the plant in a juvenile state or growing in low light.
Apply at a reduced rate once a month during the spring and summer growing season.

paragraphs.heading: Why Arrowhead Vine Leaves Turn Green
paragraphs.text: Green or reverting leaves indicate that the plant is not receiving enough light.

paragraphs.heading: Pink-hued petioles
paragraphs.text: Green leaves with mottled, lemon-yellow to lime-green variegation

paragraphs.heading: Dark-green leaf margins
paragraphs.text: Each leaf has a unique pattern of dark-green, light-green, and white variegation

paragraphs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Does arrowhead vine grow in low light?

paragraphs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Yes. Arrowhead vine tolerates low light but prefers medium to bright indirect light. Variegated varieties maintain their color better in brighter light, while leaf color may dull in lower light.

paragraphs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: What fertilizer is best for arrowhead vine?

paragraphs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Arrowhead vine is not a heavy feeder. Fertilize with a balanced fertilizer, such as 20-20-20 or 10-10-10 , at a reduced rate once a month during the spring and summer growing season.

paragraphs.heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Arrowhead Vine
paragraphs.text: Variegated arrowhead vines require brighter light to maintain their coloration. If a plant receives too little light, the leaves may revert to solid green. Moving the plant to a brighter location will encourage variegation to return on new growth.
